nodes.label: Release Workflow Job (on push tag v*)
nodes.norm_label: release workflow job (on push tag v*)

nodes.label: False calls edges from bare-symbol resolution
nodes.rationale: The AST pass resolved calls edges by bare symbol name, so every unqualified `New(` was wired to generator.New. Verified false edges: renderTemplateString -> template.New, generateSQLCRepository -> errors.New, the two identical-template tests -> template.New, validateComponent -> errors.New. Consequence: three of the six communities New() appeared to bridge (sqlc Repository Code-Gen, Component Generator Tests, CLI Command Wiring) are not connected to it at all, and its 0.254 betweenness is inflated.
nodes.norm_label: false calls edges from bare-symbol resolution

nodes.label: generator.New() as the up-front validation gate
nodes.rationale: New() is a 13-line validation gate before any template path is resolved: three whitelist checks (frameworks, databases, DI), then a FuncMap and the struct — no I/O, no file list. It is the only cheap place to reject an unsupported option, which is why the CLI wants the early error, the matrix tests want a fast assertion point that renders nothing, and the docs want one function to name for up-front rejection. Louvain even assigned New() to the test-matrix community rather than its own file's, because 15 verified test edges outweigh its 3 same-package edges.
nodes.norm_label: generator.new() as the up-front validation gate

nodes.label: CI Test job (go test -short)
nodes.rationale: -short skips the render-then-vet matrix and real-toolchain bootstraps, which need sqlc, wire, buf and a lot of memory; those run locally via make test-all.

nodes.label: CI Lint job (golangci-lint v2.11.4, pinned)
nodes.rationale: Pinned so a golangci-lint release cannot change the verdict.

nodes.label: GoReleaser cross-platform build
nodes.rationale: CGO_ENABLED=0 static nova binary for linux/darwin/windows x amd64/arm64; ldflags inject main.version and main.commit; go mod tidy runs as a before-hook.

nodes.label: Version-less release archive names
nodes.rationale: No version in the archive name because the README links to releases/latest/download/<name>, which only resolves for a stable asset name; windows uses zip.

nodes.label: golangci-lint golden config (maratori, v2.4.0 base)
nodes.rationale: Very strict but not extremely strict lint set adopted from Marat Reymers' gist; mirrored into generated projects.

nodes.label: Lint analyzer concurrency cap (4)
nodes.rationale: Default uses every CPU and a cold run spikes well past 1 GB, which swaps a 16 GB machine when anything else builds.

nodes.label: goimports + golines formatters (max-len 120)
nodes.rationale: goimports local-prefixes is still the template placeholder github.com/my/project rather than nova's module path.

nodes.label: depguard import deny-list
nodes.rationale: Denies github.com/golang/protobuf, satori uuid and pre-v5 gofrs/uuid everywhere; math/rand outside tests (use math/rand/v2); log outside main.go (use log/slog).

nodes.label: Working principles (think, simplicity, surgical, goal-driven)
nodes.rationale: Adapted from andrej-karpathy-skills to bias toward caution; goal-driven means make lint/make test stay green and generator changes are proven by make test-all with the matrix case added in the same change.

nodes.label: CLI control flow (main.go → cmd.Execute → cobra root)
nodes.rationale: root.go wires subcommands and calls locale.NewMapping once; new.go builds ProjectConfig from flags or prompts, validates, refuses non-empty dirs without --force; add.go loads the manifest and confines output under the root.
nodes.norm_label: cli control flow (main.go → cmd.execute → cobra root)

nodes.label: embed.FS text/template rendering with go/format
nodes.rationale: Files are selected by cond booleans in buildFileList; every rendered .go file passes through go/format so conditional template lines cannot leave output un-gofmt'd.

nodes.label: Variant-prefixed template naming convention
nodes.rationale: All framework/DB variants coexist (e.g. fiber_handler.go.tmpl → handler.go); the generator picks one at render time, so adding a framework means adding every prefixed template plus the option-set value.

nodes.label: ProjectConfig as single source of truth
nodes.rationale: Templates and buildFileList condition only on ProjectConfig helpers (HasHTTP, HasSQL, UseWire...); add a helper before using it. Validate() in options.go is the single gate and normalizes DBDriver/QueryGen.
nodes.norm_label: projectconfig as single source of truth

nodes.label: Component layout manifest (nova add)
nodes.rationale: manifest.Load finds the nearest go.mod root and overlays nova.yaml on Default(), so add works in projects not generated by nova new; SupportedComponents must stay in lockstep with dispatchAdd and the Generate* methods.

nodes.label: Field-driven sqlc repository generator
nodes.rationale: AST-parses the existing entity to emit migration, query, typed impl and mapper per engine; this is why GenerateEntity emits a typed port. Verify with real sqlc, not just go vet.

nodes.label: skel/ template tree (one dir per add command)
nodes.rationale: nova add templates are kept separate from the nova new tree; Generate* methods build renderSpec lists and render them with shared tmplData.
nodes.norm_label: skel/ template tree (one dir per add command)

nodes.label: GenerateWorker runnable worker scaffold
nodes.rationale: Boots through di.InitializeWorker, byte-identical to nova new's app/worker.go (TestWorkerAppTemplatesIdentical); di symbols written only when absent (diPkgDeclares) so re-runs never duplicate; assumes a nova-new or nova.yaml layout.

nodes.label: Resource limits (one heavy toolchain command at a time)
nodes.rationale: One go vet/build of a rendered project peaks near 1.1 GB and a cold golangci-lint near 1.2 GB; several at once swap a 16 GB machine, so heavy commands run serially and never in parallel subagents.
nodes.norm_label: resource limits (one heavy toolchain command at a time)

nodes.label: make test-all (render-then-vet matrix + real-toolchain bootstraps)
nodes.rationale: 36-case vet matrix plus TestGeneratedProjectBootstrap running make gen → go build → golangci-lint on eight projects; the proof required for generator/template changes.

nodes.label: Template and lint conventions
nodes.rationale: Templates are .tmpl and receive *config.ProjectConfig; files 0o600, dirs 0o750; strict lint; docs are the design reference but the template wins on disagreement.

nodes.label: graphify knowledge-graph tool
nodes.rationale: Code is tree-sitter parsed locally (no LLM cost); docs go through semantic extraction; edges are tagged EXTRACTED or INFERRED so the graph is auditable.

nodes.label: Committed graphify-out/ graph
nodes.rationale: graph.json is tracked so a fresh clone can query immediately; branches can conflict on it, resolved by taking a side and rebuilding or via graphify's union merge driver.

nodes.label: graphify post-commit rebuild hook
nodes.rationale: Per-developer install; rebuilds code-only AST extraction in a detached process; docs/*.md changes are not picked up and need /graphify . --update.

nodes.label: Graph shrink guard
nodes.rationale: Refuses to overwrite graph.json with a smaller graph to catch half-broken extractions; --force or GRAPHIFY_FORCE=1 for intentional shrinks.

nodes.label: Absolute-path sidecar gotcha (.graphify_root, .graphify_python)
nodes.rationale: Tracked sidecars hold the builder's absolute paths; .graphify_root is read by the hook rebuild as the scan root, so they should be gitignored and deleted locally after cloning.

nodes.label: nova new command
nodes.rationale: Any flag skips all prompts, so a flag-driven run must pass --transport; a worker also needs --queue and a SQL --database.

nodes.label: nova add command
nodes.rationale: Stubs are intentionally minimal; names must be Go identifiers, writes stay under the project root, and feature files are not overwritten without --force.

nodes.label: nova add worker (runnable worker service)
nodes.rationale: Refused when no kafka/rabbitmq broker is detected because the consumer is wired to that package; shared files written only when absent so a second add only appends a feature handler.

nodes.label: sqlc-backed repository scaffolding
nodes.rationale: Entity must exist first because its fields drive the columns; unsupported field types are skipped with a warning so the output always compiles.

nodes.label: nova.yaml layout manifest
nodes.rationale: Lets add target non-nova layouts via {lower}/{snake}/{title}/{db}/{cache} placeholders; without it add falls back to a fiber/postgres/wire stack.

nodes.label: Template wins over doc rule
nodes.rationale: When a doc and a template disagree the doc is the bug and is fixed in the same change, keeping templates consistent as variants are added.

nodes.label: Docs 05-12 as pattern reference, not inventory
nodes.rationale: domain/valueobject, domain/service, domain/event, adapter/external and transport/cronjob are documented for growth but not scaffolded by nova new.
nodes.norm_label: docs 05-12 as pattern reference, not inventory

nodes.label: Interactive prompts and flag mapping
nodes.rationale: --db-driver, --query and --config have no prompt because only one value is implemented per engine; Validate fills them in.

nodes.label: Up-front config validation (ProjectConfig.Validate)
nodes.rationale: Runs before any file is written and again in generator.New so code-built configs cannot bypass it; rejects unimplemented values (cron, cli, nethttp, sqlite, mongodb, sqlx, gorm, raw, bigcache, nats, toml, env) and lists every problem at once.

nodes.label: --database=none in-memory UserRepository
nodes.rationale: Keeps User CRUD, handlers and the DI graph building and running without a database; health probe mirrors liveness.

nodes.label: Elasticsearch typedapi lint-time cost
nodes.rationale: Importing root go-elasticsearch/v8 links thousands of typedapi types, making golangci-lint take 6-8 minutes vs 19 seconds; nova's own bootstrap keeps Search off for this reason.

nodes.label: Mutually exclusive transports
nodes.rationale: Transport is a single string, so no one run emits cmd/api.go, cmd/grpc.go and cmd/worker.go together; the tree is a union marked [HTTP]/[gRPC]/[worker].

nodes.label: HTTP envelope vs writer split
nodes.rationale: Framework-free envelope lives in pkg/httputil; the framework-bound writer lives in transport/http/httpwriter; locale reaches both via context.Context.

nodes.label: observability Logger port in pkg/
nodes.rationale: Port in pkg/observability, zerolog impl in infrastructure/logger, so usecase and adapter code log via logctx.From(ctx) without importing infrastructure.

nodes.label: jwt/ in infrastructure, not adapter
nodes.rationale: Signing and verifying are pure computation and verification is called only by auth middleware, so it belongs with technical bootstrapping.

nodes.label: TxManager interface/implementation split
nodes.rationale: Interface in domain/, implementation in adapter/repository/<db>/, so usecases inject domain.TxManager without knowing the DB.

nodes.label: make gen order (sqlc → buf → tidy → wire)
nodes.rationale: dbgen/, api/gen/ and wire_gen.go are not rendered; generators run first so tidy sees their imports, wire last because it type-checks the injector against a tidied module.
nodes.norm_label: make gen order (sqlc → buf → tidy → wire)

nodes.label: Dependency Rule (dependencies point inward)
nodes.rationale: Domain has zero external deps; usecase depends only on domain and pkg/ (pinned by TestDependencyRule); adapters never depend on usecase; infrastructure depends on all inner layers.

nodes.label: Dependency Inversion (interfaces in domain)
nodes.rationale: High-level usecases define interfaces, low-level repositories implement them; the only exception is the cross-cutting observability.Logger in pkg/.

nodes.label: Adapter vs Infrastructure decision guide
nodes.rationale: Adapter fulfils domain ports by running business operations on external systems; infrastructure provides technical capabilities (pools, servers, config, DI); code importing nothing under internal/ goes to pkg/.

nodes.label: Ports implemented outside adapter/
nodes.rationale: Satisfying a port is necessary but not sufficient for adapter/; TokenIssuer (jwt), PasswordHasher (bcrypt) and observability.Logger (zerolog) live in infrastructure because they do no business I/O.

nodes.label: middleware/ under transport/http, interceptors under transport/grpc
nodes.rationale: HTTP middleware and gRPC interceptors have different signatures; each transport owns its cross-cutting concerns so removing gRPC is just deleting transport/grpc/.
nodes.norm_label: middleware/ under transport/http, interceptors under transport/grpc

nodes.label: httpwriter under transport/http, not pkg/
nodes.rationale: The writer is framework-coupled and transport-specific; general rule: a package importing internal/ or a specific framework must live inside internal/.

nodes.label: pkg/locale shared error codes
nodes.rationale: Pragmatic trade-off: usecases return errors.L(locale.Code) instead of domain error types mapped per transport, avoiding duplicated mapping at the cost of coupling usecases to the error-code system.

nodes.label: transport/ as sibling of adapter/ (inbound vs outbound)
nodes.rationale: Handlers are adapters in theory, but are separated for scale, team ownership and a clean deletion boundary; adapter/ is outbound, transport/ is inbound.
nodes.norm_label: transport/ as sibling of adapter/ (inbound vs outbound)

nodes.label: pkg/ vs internal/shared/
nodes.rationale: pkg/ has no compiler meaning; it is used as a well-known convention to visually separate shared utilities from layered code, though internal/shared/ is equally valid for a private service.

nodes.label: Consumer owns the interface
nodes.rationale: If a usecase calls an adapter, its interface lives in domain/ (one file per concern); if only transport calls it, no domain interface is defined.

nodes.label: security.TokenIssuer port (shipped variant)
nodes.rationale: DI binds *jwtsec.TokenService to the port so usecase/ imports nothing from infrastructure/; Login tests run against a two-line fake issuer.

nodes.label: JWT verification without a domain interface
nodes.rationale: Verification is a middleware concern that puts the principal in context before the handler; the usecase never verifies tokens, so the auth middleware uses TokenService directly.
nodes.norm_label: jwt verification without a domain interface

nodes.label: entity.User
nodes.rationale: No framework or json tags because serialization is a transport concern; the stored credential is PasswordHash, never plaintext.

nodes.label: NewUser / Rename entity invariants
nodes.rationale: The entity owns its invariants so every transport (HTTP, gRPC, worker, nova add output) inherits them instead of restating validate tags; violations are ErrEmailInvalid/ErrNameInvalid, mapped to 400 by the usecase. HTTP validate tags remain only as a fast first line.

nodes.label: Value objects (not scaffolded)
nodes.rationale: Enforce invariants at construction, eliminate primitive obsession, make signatures self-documenting; equal by attributes, not identity.

nodes.label: valueobject.Money
nodes.rationale: Amount in smallest unit plus ISO 4217 currency so mixed-currency math is rejected.

nodes.label: domain.UserRepository port
nodes.rationale: Lives in package domain, one file per aggregate (port + filter), avoiding the repository.UserRepository stutter and a messy shared port.go.

nodes.label: Two read shapes: List+Count vs ListAfter
nodes.rationale: Separate methods so the cursor path never runs COUNT(*) and the admin path never fakes totals; the port returns no result struct, the usecase composes its own DTO.
nodes.norm_label: two read shapes: list+count vs listafter

nodes.label: Filter passthrough rule
nodes.rationale: If the usecase does zero transformation, the transport assembler maps straight to domain.UserFilter; add a usecase DTO only when it clamps, authorizes or combines data.

nodes.label: Domain service (PricingService, not scaffolded)
nodes.rationale: Cross-entity business rules and decisions are domain interfaces implemented in usecase/; multi-table JOINs are repository concerns, not domain services.

nodes.label: Return data vs return a decision test
nodes.rationale: Returns data (even across JOINs) -> repository; returns a decision or computation -> domain service. Switching Postgres to Mongo removes the JOIN but not the repository interface.
nodes.norm_label: return data vs return a decision test

nodes.label: domain.UserPublisher port + UserCreated event
nodes.rationale: Shipped with --queue; one publisher port and event struct per aggregate directly in domain/, matching domain.UserRepository.

nodes.label: event.EventPublisher port (not scaffolded)
nodes.rationale: Typed methods instead of Publish(topic, any) for compile-time safety; domain events carry no json tags (adapter maps to wire DTOs); no Close() because constructors own cleanup.

nodes.label: usersvc.Service (user usecase)
nodes.rationale: Holds only ports (UserRepository, PasswordHasher, TokenIssuer, TxManager, UserPublisher) so service_test drives it with fakes; Login lives here because authentication is a user concern in the scaffold.

nodes.label: Usecase error discipline (errors.L vs Wrapf, never log)
nodes.rationale: A violated rule returns errors.L (translatable code + status); a failed dependency returns errors.Wrapf (frame + cause). The service never logs, keeping one log line per request, except the swallowed best-effort publish.
nodes.norm_label: usecase error discipline (errors.l vs wrapf, never log)

nodes.label: Register (hash outside tx, check+insert in WithinTx)
nodes.rationale: bcrypt (~100ms) must not hold a connection; only ErrNotFound means free to create, so a DB outage during lookup propagates instead of creating a duplicate.
nodes.norm_label: register (hash outside tx, check+insert in withintx)

nodes.label: Uniqueness check is advisory; the constraint decides
nodes.rationale: Two concurrent registers can both pass the check; the unique index raises, the adapter translates to ErrAlreadyExists, and the usecase returns the same UserEmailExists 409, never a 500.
nodes.norm_label: uniqueness check is advisory; the constraint decides

nodes.label: Best-effort event publish
nodes.rationale: The user is already persisted, so a broker outage must not fail the request; the swallowed error is logged to drive alerts. Guaranteed delivery would need an outbox, not a retry loop.

nodes.label: List (page-based, policy clamped in usecase)
nodes.rationale: Defaults and caps (10/500) live in the usecase so every transport inherits one policy; page query and Count share one WithinTx; clamped values are echoed back in ListOutput.

nodes.label: PublicList (cursor/keyset paging)
nodes.rationale: Reads limit+1 to learn HasMore, opaque base64 cursor, keyset stable under concurrent inserts, projects the display name only so anonymous callers cannot harvest emails; a malformed cursor is a 400.

nodes.label: Login uniform failure and timing (timingHash)
nodes.rationale: Unknown user and bad password both return InvalidCredentials; the unknown-user path runs a bcrypt verify against a lazily built dummy hash so wall-clock timing cannot enumerate accounts; fails closed if the hash cannot be built.

nodes.label: requireSelf ownership check
nodes.rationale: Update/Delete: no principal -> 401, another user's id -> 403; lives in the usecase so future gRPC or CLI transports inherit it.

nodes.label: Usecase DTOs (Output, ListOutput, PublicOutput, LoginOutput)
nodes.rationale: Plain structs without tags; entities never cross the usecase boundary and transport owns json/validate.

nodes.label: svc import alias convention (usersvc)
nodes.rationale: The usecase package shares its name with the transport feature package, so it is always imported with a svc suffix, never the bare name.

nodes.label: pricing.Service (domain service implementation)
nodes.rationale: Pure business logic with no external system, so the implementation lives in usecase/; injected into usecases, never called from handlers.

nodes.label: Repository vs domain service vs usecase
nodes.rationale: Returns data -> repository; returns a decision with no I/O -> domain service; orchestrates side effects -> usecase.
nodes.norm_label: repository vs domain service vs usecase

nodes.label: useraudit RecordUserCreated (record each event once)
nodes.rationale: The broker delivers at least once: eventId is stored under a unique index, ErrEventAlreadyRecorded is treated as success with one 'duplicate delivery ignored' line, other errors are returned for the worker policy to retry and park.

nodes.label: transport/http.NewRouter
nodes.rationale: Builds the framework instance only; port binding and shutdown belong to infrastructure/server. Registrars are a slice, not a map, so mount order is deterministic.

nodes.label: Load-bearing middleware order
nodes.rationale: ClientIP -> OTel -> RequestID -> Logging -> Recovery -> Timeout -> BodyLimit -> CORS -> Locale: later layers see trace and request IDs, panics still produce an access line, deadline panics are caught.

nodes.label: v1.Prefixed / APIPrefix (/api/v1)
nodes.rationale: The prefix is declared once per API section and shared by embedding rather than restated per feature.

nodes.label: Per-feature transport package (dto, assembler, handler, registrar)
nodes.rationale: Keeps one endpoint group together and scales past 10+ features; deleting a feature is deleting a directory; dto.go and assembler.go are framework-free.
nodes.norm_label: per-feature transport package (dto, assembler, handler, registrar)

nodes.label: Transport validation is shape, not policy
nodes.rationale: Formats and enums belong to the wire contract; magnitudes like perPage caps are usecase policy so gRPC and CLI inherit the same limits.
nodes.norm_label: transport validation is shape, not policy

nodes.label: assembler.go projections (usecase -> wire)
nodes.rationale: The only place that maps; data and meta are separate projections because the envelope keeps them in separate fields.

nodes.label: HTTP user Handler
nodes.rationale: Never logs, uses c.UserContext() not c.Context(), normalizes with errors.ToAppError, no status literals; Delete returns 204 without envelope.

nodes.label: user Registrar (auth boundary at group level)
nodes.rationale: One Auth middleware per protected group so a new protected route cannot forget it; tokenSvc and loginLimit arrive via the constructor so the limiter state is per-instance and testable.
nodes.norm_label: user registrar (auth boundary at group level)

nodes.label: httpwriter.WriteError
nodes.rationale: The single funnel every error passes through: stashes the AppError for the Logging middleware, translates by ctx language, writes the envelope with status from AppError.Code.

nodes.label: httpwriter.Bind / BindQuery / ParseID
nodes.rationale: Every parse or validation failure becomes the same generic localized 400 so clients cannot probe field names; the cause rides along via WithCause for the access log.

nodes.label: RequestID middleware
nodes.rationale: Reuses an inbound X-Request-ID only if requestid.Valid accepts it, otherwise mints a UUID.

nodes.label: Logging middleware (one access line per request)
nodes.rationale: c.Path() not OriginalURL() keeps query secrets out of logs; probes and OPTIONS emit no line; level follows status; route and user_id (via principal slot) on the access line.
nodes.norm_label: logging middleware (one access line per request)

nodes.label: Recovery middleware
nodes.rationale: Fiber buffers responses so no wroteHeader flag is needed; net/http variants track written headers to avoid corrupting a partial response.

nodes.label: CORS middleware (empty list installs nothing)
nodes.rationale: fiber and echo read an empty origin list as '*', so the middleware is not installed when empty; gin and chi add Vary: Origin.

nodes.label: Locale middleware (Accept-Language)
nodes.rationale: Unknown languages degrade to English rather than erroring; translation is delegated entirely to pkg/locale.

nodes.label: Auth middleware (bearer token -> principal)
nodes.rationale: Case-insensitive scheme, RFC 6750 challenges on every 401; the usecase reads the principal via identity and never learns JWT exists.

nodes.label: LoginRateLimit (per-IP token bucket)
nodes.rationale: 5/min burst 5 with Retry-After, idle buckets evicted so memory tracks recent clients; per-process, so N replicas allow Nx — raises credential-stuffing cost, not a WAF substitute.

nodes.label: ClientIP middleware (trusted proxies)
nodes.rationale: Believes X-Forwarded-For only through http.trusted_proxies so the access log and the login limiter read the same non-spoofable client IP; fiber's c.IP() would return the header verbatim.

nodes.label: health.Checker (Liveness/Readiness)
nodes.rationale: Liveness is never coupled to the DB (a blip would restart every healthy pod); Readiness pings DB and Redis under one 1s deadline with per-check details.

nodes.label: transport/grpc.New (gRPC server factory)
nodes.rationale: Shaped like transport/http: server factory instead of router, interceptors instead of middleware, rpcstatus instead of httpwriter; health reports process liveness only.

nodes.label: gRPC Registrar (Register/Public/Throttled)
nodes.rationale: Auth is deny-by-default: a new RPC needs a token until listed in Public(), checked by TestEveryRPCIsProtectedUnlessPublic.

nodes.label: rpcstatus.FromError (AppError -> gRPC status)
nodes.rationale: Single error path: ToAppError, stash for the access log, translate, map HTTP status to the nearest gRPC code so internal error text never reaches the client.

nodes.label: gRPC interceptor chain
nodes.rationale: RequestID -> Locale -> Logging -> Recovery -> Deadline -> Throttle -> Auth mirror the HTTP middleware; unary only; Throttle keys on the TCP peer since gRPC has no X-Forwarded-For convention.

nodes.label: transport/worker Worker orchestrator
nodes.rationale: Mirrors transport/http: topic-keyed handler map, broker consumer chosen at generation time; dispatch adopts traceparent/x-request-id and emits one handled|parked|abandoned line.

nodes.label: worker.Policy (timeout, attempts, backoff)
nodes.rationale: Per-attempt deadline and panic guard, retries with doubling backoff, parks on Poison or spent budget; shutdown returns ctx.Err() so dispatch has exactly three outcomes.

nodes.label: worker.Poison
nodes.rationale: Input that can never succeed is parked at once; transient errors are retried then parked; never swallow an error to keep the partition moving.

nodes.label: Delivery settlement (ack / dead-letter / redeliver)
nodes.rationale: Kafka copies parked messages to <topic>.dlq then marks; RabbitMQ nacks to <queue>.dlx; ConsumeClaim never returns on handler or DLQ-write failure, which used to rebalance the group on every poison message.

nodes.label: Duplicated topic constant (user.created)
nodes.rationale: A shared constant would couple the consumer module to the producer; duplication with a pointer comment keeps the worker separable into its own service.

nodes.label: transport/cronjob (not scaffolded)
nodes.rationale: A schedule is a delivery mechanism, so cron handlers are thin transport wrappers over a usecase; cron.go.tmpl exists but is not wired into buildFileList.

nodes.label: Three-file SQL repository (tx_manager, qx, repository)
nodes.rationale: A repository method must join an ambient transaction without knowing whether one is running.

nodes.label: TxManager.WithinTx
nodes.rationale: Unconditional deferred Rollback guarantees no leaked connection even on panic; nested calls reuse the ambient tx so composed usecases cannot self-deadlock; unexported txKey struct{}.

nodes.label: qx TX-aware query executor
nodes.rationale: Q(ctx) binds dbgen.Queries to the ctx tx or falls back to the pool; unexported and held as a field, not embedded, so Q is not promoted onto the repository.

nodes.label: postgres/mysql UserRepository
nodes.rationale: Translating pgx.ErrNoRows/sql.ErrNoRows to errors.ErrNotFound is the adapter's job and the reason it is an adapter, not infrastructure; constructor takes the pool so DI never sees qx.

nodes.label: translate (unique violation 23505/1062 -> ErrAlreadyExists)
nodes.rationale: Keeps the driver error wrapped so the access log shows the constraint; unit-tested without a database.

nodes.label: mapper package (row <-> entity)
nodes.rationale: Pure functions absorb the storage-vs-domain naming gap (password column vs PasswordHash) and keep pgtype from escaping the package; unit-testable without a DB.

nodes.label: sqlc.yaml (schema from migrations)
nodes.rationale: sqlc reads the migration files as schema so there is exactly one table definition; jsonb maps to json.RawMessage so the mapper need not re-encode.

nodes.label: users migration (TIMESTAMPTZ, UNIQUE email)
nodes.rationale: TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE avoids one-hour bugs; the UNIQUE email constraint is the real uniqueness guarantee; mysql uses BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT and DATETIME(6).

nodes.label: sqlc.arg optional-filter idiom
nodes.rationale: An optional filter stays a single prepared statement: no string concatenation, no SQL injection surface, one query plan; CountUsers shares the email arg while ignoring limit/offset.

nodes.label: ListUsersAfter keyset query
nodes.rationale: id > cursor ORDER BY id LIMIT n with no OFFSET, so cost does not grow with page depth.

nodes.label: pubsub.Publisher (event publisher adapter)
nodes.rationale: Split into user_message.go, user_publisher.go and broker-specific publisher.go so swapping kafka/rabbitmq touches one file; exported surface identical so DI never changes; partition key is the user id.

nodes.label: UserCreatedMessage wire DTO (eventId)
nodes.rationale: Producer-minted eventId is the consumer's idempotency key, also sent as the x-event-id header so dead letters can be matched without decoding.

nodes.label: UserCacheRepository (Redis cache-aside decorator)
nodes.rationale: Wraps UserRepository; GetByEmail bypasses the cache because login needs PasswordHash; every cache failure degrades to the DB; TTL jitter; lists not cached; not wired by default because caching is a domain decision.

nodes.label: Elasticsearch user index (derived read model)
nodes.rationale: SQL stays the system of record; Search returns IDs hydrated via SQL so the index cannot serve stale fields; not wired by default because sync on every write is an opt-in burden.

nodes.label: memory UserRepository + no-op TxManager
nodes.rationale: For --database=none, so the usecase constructor stays the same without a database.

nodes.label: Ports implemented outside adapter/
nodes.rationale: TokenIssuer, PasswordHasher and observability.Logger are satisfied in infrastructure because signing/hashing are pure computation and logging is cross-cutting; satisfying a port is necessary but not sufficient for adapter/.

nodes.label: (instance, cleanup, error) constructor contract
nodes.rationale: Each component owns its own shutdown; no Close() on domain ports and no central teardown; DI composes cleanups in reverse order so adding a dependency cannot leak it.

nodes.label: Constructors verify connectivity (fail fast)
nodes.rationale: A misconfigured dependency fails at startup, not on the first production request; Redis is the exception and starts degraded because a cache outage is survivable.

nodes.label: config.Load (embedded YAML + env overrides)
nodes.rationale: YAML is go:embed-ed so the binary has no cwd dependency (config change = rebuild); APP_ENV whitelisted so a typo fails at startup; DB_USER required; lists trimmed by normalizeLists.

nodes.label: Config precedence: base.yaml -> <APP_ENV>.yaml -> .env -> env vars
nodes.rationale: loadDotEnv sets only keys absent from the environment so host runs work and containers keep injecting env; an empty KEY= keeps the YAML default.

nodes.label: YAML vs .env split by nature
nodes.rationale: Operational tuning lives in reviewed YAML; secrets and per-deploy endpoints live in env; JWT keys carry only env tags so they cannot be committed by accident.

nodes.label: Sub-config projection
nodes.rationale: Constructors take only the sub-struct they read, so signatures document dependencies and nothing quietly depends on an unrelated section; NewRouter is the one exception.

nodes.label: Inverted insecure-by-default (CORS, trusted_proxies, tracing)
nodes.rationale: An unconfigured deployment rejects all cross-origin traffic and ignores forwarded headers — visibly broken rather than invisibly unsafe; empty tracing endpoint means no-op tracer.

nodes.label: Escape-safe DSN assembly (net/url, mysql.Config.FormatDSN)
nodes.rationale: Discrete typed DB fields instead of DATABASE_URL; a fmt.Sprintf DSN breaks the moment a rotated password contains @ : / ? # or a space.

nodes.label: cache.Client / search.Client thin wrappers
nodes.rationale: The wrapper makes single/sentinel/cluster a config choice rather than a code change; embedding redis.UniversalClient keeps the full API.

nodes.label: NewKafkaProducer (sync, WaitForAll)
nodes.rationale: Synchronous fully-acknowledged producer because a silently dropped ack would defeat best-effort-with-logging; dials at startup since an unreachable broker is misconfiguration, not degraded mode.

nodes.label: NewKafkaConsumerGroup (OffsetOldest, fail fast)
nodes.rationale: Fails fast without consumer_group_id; OffsetOldest replays history on a fresh group instead of skipping; group membership gives automatic rebalancing; the factory does no consuming.

nodes.label: NewRabbitMQConnection / NewRabbitMQChannel
nodes.rationale: Shared default exchange 'events' lets a separately generated publisher and worker meet without edits; Kafka topic names are wire contracts, not config.

nodes.label: HTTPServer lifecycle wrapper
nodes.rationale: Shutdown ctx rooted at context.Background(): deriving it from the signal-cancelled ctx collapses ShutdownTimeout to zero and kills in-flight requests.

nodes.label: zerolog Logger (implements observability.Logger)
nodes.rationale: Instance-based, never a global; callerSkip=2 so caller points at the real call site; stamps service/version/env; first line 'config loaded' with a redacted Summary.

nodes.label: jwtsec TokenService (RS256)
nodes.rationale: RS256 not HS256: with a shared HMAC secret any verifier can forge; only the issuer holds the private key; package named jwtsec to avoid colliding with golang-jwt; small surface (Sign, ParseAndVerifyAccessToken, AccessTokenTTL).

nodes.label: Generic 401 with severity-triaged verify logging
nodes.rationale: Telling a caller why a token failed is an oracle; expired/malformed go to Debug, invalid signature, issuer/audience mismatch or unknown errors go to Warn.

nodes.label: BcryptHasher (clamped cost)
nodes.rationale: Invalid cost clamps to DefaultCost instead of failing boot and never yields cost 0; Verify collapses every mismatch to ErrUnauthorized.

nodes.label: OpenTelemetry tracing provider
nodes.rationale: An empty endpoint yields a no-op tracer that still installs the propagator, so one hop without a collector does not break a distributed trace; Shutdown flushes pending spans.

nodes.label: Adapter vs infrastructure test
nodes.rationale: Creates a client, binds a port or computes purely -> infrastructure; uses a client to fulfil a domain port or translates driver errors -> adapter.

nodes.label: pkg/ rule: no internal/, no framework imports
nodes.rationale: What makes pkg/ legitimate rather than a dumping ground.
nodes.norm_label: pkg/ rule: no internal/, no framework imports

nodes.label: pkg/errors
nodes.rationale: HTTP-focused AppErrors with a caller-info trace for one-line logging; non-goals: no stack dumps, no status codes on Wrap, no language in business code.

nodes.label: AppError
nodes.rationale: Args and Err are json:'-' because args may contain user data and the cause is diagnostic: the client sees a translated message, the operator sees the cause.

nodes.label: Error sentinels (ErrNotFound, ErrAlreadyExists, ...)
nodes.rationale: The adapter-to-usecase vocabulary: the usecase checks errors.Is without knowing the driver; std helpers re-exported so one errors import suffices.

nodes.label: errors.L constructor
nodes.rationale: Derives HTTP status from the locale code and captures one frame; returns *AppError since it is never nil and chains WithCause.

nodes.label: errors.Wrap / Wrapf
nodes.rationale: Classify once at the originating layer: Wrap appends a frame and preserves existing classification; returns error, not *AppError, so Wrap(nil) is a true nil instead of a typed-nil pointer.

nodes.label: AppError.WithCause
nodes.rationale: Attaches a diagnostic cause without changing client-facing classification; surfaces only in the access log's app_err/app_trace.

nodes.label: Frame trail (Frames / Origin / Trace)
nodes.rationale: runtime.Caller per wrap instead of a full stack: the path the error took through your layers is the part you read; shortFile matches the logger's caller format.

nodes.label: localeHTTPStatus table
nodes.rationale: Single source of truth mapping locale code to status for both L() and classify() so they cannot drift; a missing code silently resolves to 500; framework-free so gRPC/worker reuse it.

nodes.label: errors.FromStatus
nodes.rationale: Inverse of the table for framework-raised 404/405/413 so they use the same envelope; unmapped statuses become 500 instead of leaking the framework message.

nodes.label: classify / ToAppError
nodes.rationale: Always locale-coded: LocaleError -> its code, sentinel -> canonical code, anything else -> InternalError, so third-party error text never reaches a client; DeadlineExceeded -> 504.

nodes.label: errors.LogFields
nodes.rationale: Uses the same field names as the HTTP access log (app_code, app_err, app_trace, app_locale) so one query works across HTTP and worker logs.

nodes.label: AppError context stash (PrepareAppErrorContext / StashAppError)
nodes.rationale: A mutable pointer slot in ctx carries the error upward through an immutable context to the Logging middleware — what buys 'handlers never log'; no-ops when absent.

nodes.label: pkg/locale
nodes.rationale: Codes and text here, status in pkg/errors, so a non-HTTP transport uses the same codes.

nodes.label: Locale codes (negative ints, banded by feature)
nodes.rationale: Negative so they cannot be confused with HTTP status; banded (-1000 general, -1100 user) so a new aggregate claims a range.
nodes.norm_label: locale codes (negative ints, banded by feature)

nodes.label: LocaleError (code + raw args)
nodes.rationale: Args are stored raw and substituted at translation time, so business code never names a language.

nodes.label: locale.NewMapping / Translate
nodes.rationale: No init() side effects so registration is explicit and testable; Translate falls back to English per string, then 'unknown error: %d'.

nodes.label: Language in context (WithLanguage / LanguageFromContext)
nodes.rationale: Key and accessors live in pkg/locale so pkg/httputil and pkg/errors can read the language without importing transport code.

nodes.label: pkg/httputil response envelope
nodes.rationale: Framework-free envelope {success, data, error, meta, requestId}; requestId in the body turns a user's report into a full server-side log replay.

nodes.label: CursorMeta
nodes.rationale: User-facing keyset paging meta; deliberately exposes no totals because counting every match defeats the point.

nodes.label: PageMeta / NewPageMeta
nodes.rationale: Admin offset/page meta requiring a COUNT; reserved for back-office lists; NewPageMeta avoids divide-by-zero.

nodes.label: ErrorResponseFromApp
nodes.rationale: HTTP status says category, error.code (the locale code) says reason so clients branch without string matching; a nil app still yields a translated 500.

nodes.label: pkg/requestid (transport-neutral correlation ID)
nodes.rationale: HTTP middleware, gRPC interceptor and worker dispatcher all set it; publishers copy it onto outgoing messages as x-request-id; carriers stay with their transports.

nodes.label: observability.Logger port
nodes.rationale: Port in pkg/, implementation in infrastructure/logger, so a usecase logs without importing infrastructure; reserved keys time/level/caller/message; tracing and metrics deliberately have no port.

nodes.label: pkg/logctx (request-scoped logger)
nodes.rationale: From never returns nil (Nop fallback), so inner layers log inline without guards; depends only on the port, keeping usecase -> logctx -> observability.

nodes.label: cmd.Execute (cobra root)
nodes.rationale: Calls locale.NewMapping once before any subcommand so even CLI commands that never build DI get translations; SilenceUsage; exit 1 on error.

nodes.label: RunE, not Run
nodes.rationale: Returning the error lets cobra set the exit code; os.Exit inside a command would skip deferred DI cleanup (pool close, span flush).

nodes.label: app.RunHTTPServer lifecycle
nodes.rationale: signal.NotifyContext owns shutdown; Start runs in a goroutine; http.ErrServerClosed is not an error; errChan buffered to avoid a goroutine leak; cleanup deferred right after Initialize succeeds.

nodes.label: app.RunWorker
nodes.rationale: A consume loop that returns while ctx is live (nil or ErrConsumerClosed) is fatal so the orchestrator restarts it; drains up to 30s before Stop; byte-identical to nova add worker output.

nodes.label: HTTPApp / GRPCApp / WorkerApp bundles
nodes.rationale: Returns the same logger DI wired everywhere; Tracer field listed before Server forces the tracing provider (and its flush) into the graph and makes it clean up last; the struct also prunes the graph per binary.

nodes.label: provideRegistrars / provideWorkerHandlers (extension points)
nodes.rationale: Adding a feature means adding its constructor to a set and its instance to one of these slices; slice order is mount order.

nodes.label: Wire provider sets (infraSet, httpInfraSet, grpcInfraSet, workerInfraSet, ...)
nodes.rationale: Layered and unexported; Wire builds only what the injector's App struct reaches, so a worker never builds TokenService or needs JWT keys.
nodes.norm_label: wire provider sets (infraset, httpinfraset, grpcinfraset, workerinfraset, ...)

nodes.label: wire.Bind (port -> implementation)
nodes.rationale: Where dependency inversion is actually executed: the only place that says 'postgres'; swapping in the cache decorator changes exactly one line.

nodes.label: Initialize* injectors (InitializeHTTPServer, InitializeGRPCServer, InitializeWorker)
nodes.rationale: panic(wire.Build(...)) is a declaration replaced in wire_gen.go; run wire after editing or the binary is unchanged.

nodes.label: fx modules (Uber fx DI)
nodes.rationale: Same Initialize* signatures so internal/app is byte-identical across engines; fx resolves at runtime via reflection (no codegen), Wire at compile time; shutdown_timeout is fx's overall stop budget.

nodes.label: Reverse-construction-order cleanup
nodes.rationale: The server stops accepting requests before the pool it depends on closes; tracing flushes last; a constructor that owns a resource but returns no cleanup leaks it silently.

nodes.label: Adding a feature checklist
nodes.rationale: Skipping the wire.go step fails generation; skipping provideRegistrars compiles but never mounts the routes; nova add automates most of it.

nodes.label: Generated project Makefile
nodes.rationale: test runs -race; lint chains sqlfluff and buf lint; no make build/run because running requires choosing a subcommand; recipes use $(CURDIR) not $(PWD).

nodes.label: make gen (sqlc -> proto -> tidy -> wire)
nodes.rationale: Composed from only the generators the project has, so a fx/no-database project reduces to go mod tidy; buf plugins are version-pinned go run invocations.

nodes.label: wire-gen (deletes stale wire_gen.go, go tool wire)
nodes.rationale: A stale generated file that still compiles is worse than a missing one; the go.mod tool directive pins wire so nothing is installed.
nodes.norm_label: wire-gen (deletes stale wire_gen.go, go tool wire)

nodes.label: migrate-* targets (MIGRATE_DATABASE_URL)
nodes.rationale: Migration tooling runs outside the app so it reads a URL from env (falling back to .env); migrate-down defaults to n=1 so it never unwinds the whole schema.

nodes.label: .githooks/pre-commit (fmt, lint, build)
nodes.rationale: Opt-in via make setup; fails if fmt changed anything instead of mutating the commit; rendered executable (0o700) because git silently skips non-executable hooks.

nodes.label: Two-stage Dockerfile
nodes.rationale: Cached go mod download layer, CGO_ENABLED=0 static binary, -trimpath -w -s, non-root USER app, ca-certificates + tzdata; config is embedded so only the binary and migrations ship; ENTRYPOINT/CMD split selects the subcommand.

nodes.label: Committed generated code (wire_gen.go, dbgen, api/gen)
nodes.rationale: Keeps the image build hermetic (no wire/sqlc/buf in the builder) and makes the generated graph reviewable in a PR.

nodes.label: Docker HEALTHCHECK on /readyz
nodes.rationale: Probes readiness, not liveness, so a container that cannot reach its database is not routed traffic; transport-gated so worker images declare no port.

nodes.label: docker-compose local stack with env-var resource limits
nodes.rationale: Every limit is an env var with a default for reproducible benchmarks (Compose V2 required); environment overrides env_file so one .env serves host and network; dependencies wait on service_healthy.
nodes.norm_label: docker-compose local stack with env-var resource limits

nodes.label: Dead-letter topology (<topic>.dlq, <queue>.dlx)
nodes.rationale: Compose auto-creates Kafka dlq topics; RabbitMQ declares dlx/dlq at worker start; the dead-letter exchange is named after the queue because queue arguments are fixed at creation.

nodes.label: CI workflow (lint, tidy, test -> build)
nodes.rationale: tidy job catches go.mod drift; tests are hermetic with no service containers; golangci-lint pinned to v2.11.4 via action v8; token scoped to contents: read.

nodes.label: .env.example (secrets and per-deploy endpoints only)
nodes.rationale: Tuning is reviewed in code, secrets are injected; every value is sourceable as written; discrete DB fields, empty CORS and trusted proxies, JWT keys required.

nodes.label: Cross-cutting feature list
nodes.rationale: Templates never omit these; adding an HTTP framework variant means re-implementing the whole list for it.

nodes.label: Everything rides on context.Context
nodes.rationale: Seven ctx values, each with an unexported struct{} key; accessors live with the value, not the setter; only the AppError and principal slots are mutable, to flow values back up to the access log.

nodes.label: Log once, at the boundary
nodes.rationale: Inner layers wrap and return; one line per failed request so alerting counts requests, the frame trail replaces the stack, correlation is free. Exceptions are swallowed errors: best-effort publish, cache failures, panic recovery, duplicate delivery.

nodes.label: Classify at the origin, translate at the edge
nodes.rationale: Status decided at creation from one table so Wrapf cannot turn a 409 into a 500; language decided at the boundary; args travel raw so the same error renders in any language.
nodes.norm_label: classify at the origin, translate at the edge

nodes.label: Each component owns its shutdown
nodes.rationale: The cost: a constructor that acquires a resource without returning a cleanup leaks it silently; the benefit: adding a dependency cannot break shutdown ordering.

nodes.label: Observability at a glance
nodes.rationale: Log to trace in one click via trace_id, user report to full replay via requestId, signal over volume (probes silent, 4xx at Warn).

nodes.label: Deliberately absent features
nodes.rationale: No /metrics, no general rate limiter, no outbox, no refresh tokens, no role model, unary-only gRPC, cronjob not rendered, value objects/domain services/events documented as patterns only.

nodes.label: Nova Review Remediation Roadmap
nodes.rationale: Master plan sequencing the 2026-10-04 review findings so every supported `nova new` output builds, lints, runs and is debuggable from logs, and the CLI never silently produces a broken project or destroys user files.

nodes.label: 2026-10-04 Architecture Review of Nova
nodes.rationale: Six parallel reviewers plus hands-on verification (seven variants rendered, three bootstrapped with real sqlc, wire, go build, golangci-lint); every finding was reproduced, not just read.

nodes.label: Heavy Toolchain Serialization Rule
nodes.rationale: Heavy toolchain commands (make test-all, golangci-lint, go build/vet of rendered projects) run one at a time from the main thread, never in parallel subagents, never go clean -cache; each peaks near 1 GB and concurrent runs froze the 16 GB dev machine.

nodes.label: Four-Framework Variant Parity Rule
nodes.rationale: Every change to a *_handler, *_router, *_middleware, *_registrar or *_http template must be applied to all four framework variants (fiber, gin, chi, echo) so behavior never diverges by framework.

nodes.label: Worker Template Byte-Identity Rule
nodes.rationale: templates/app/worker.go.tmpl vs skel/worker/app_worker.go.tmpl, cmd/worker.go.tmpl vs skel/worker/cmd_worker.go.tmpl, and transport/worker/policy.go.tmpl vs skel/worker/policy.go.tmpl must stay byte-identical so `nova new` and `nova add worker` produce the same runtime.

nodes.label: Template Wins Over Doc Rule
nodes.rationale: Where a doc in docs/ and a template disagree, the template is authoritative and the doc is fixed in the same change.

nodes.label: Commit Only via /grimoire-core:commit
nodes.rationale: Commits happen only through /grimoire-core:commit after explicit user confirmation; no git commit, no --amend, no Claude co-author trailer.

nodes.label: Debuggability Scorecard (where/when/what/who/why x HTTP/worker/gRPC)
nodes.rationale: Phase 3 exit criterion: every cell 'ok' except gRPC 'who', verified by asserting field presence in rendered output and one manual run per transport.

nodes.label: Typed go-elasticsearch Client Lint Cost
nodes.rationale: golangci-lint analyzers crawl thousands of generated types: 6-8 minutes per project versus 19 seconds without it; consider the low-level esapi client or document the cost next to --search=elasticsearch.

nodes.label: Phase 0: Resource Guardrails
nodes.rationale: Verification must not freeze the 16 GB dev machine again; make test is -short, make test-all is -parallel 2 -timeout 30m, GOFLAGS -p=2, run.concurrency 4, GOGC=50 (full matrix 58 s, 0.45 GB peak warm).

nodes.label: Phase 1: Generated Output Builds and Lints
nodes.rationale: First because every later fix is verified through this harness; the matrix stubbed sqlc and wire and never rendered --database=none, which is how a non-building MySQL output and a non-compiling no-DB output shipped.
nodes.norm_label: phase 1: generated output builds and lints

nodes.label: Phase 2: CLI Hardening
nodes.rationale: Stops silent broken projects (cron, cli, toml, env, raw, gorm, typos), silent overwrites and path traversal in nova add; small and self-contained with no template churn.

nodes.label: Phase 3: Observability
nodes.rationale: The user's explicit lens: logged errors serialized to {}, trace_id was always empty, the worker failed silently; additive, low-regression changes that make every later phase easier to debug.

nodes.label: Phase 4: HTTP Transport Parity and Security
nodes.rationale: Default path for most users: CORS * fallback, no body limits, no echo timeouts, spoofable rate limiter, 404s outside the envelope.
nodes.norm_label: phase 4: http transport parity and security

nodes.label: Phase 5: Worker Reliability and Messaging
nodes.rationale: Zombie consumer on channel close, Kafka rebalance storm on one poison message, exchange-name mismatch that made the README demo undeliverable; independent of phase 4.

nodes.label: Phase 6: Layers and Domain Correctness
nodes.rationale: Usecase depended on concrete JWT type, dead TxManager, duplicate email returned 500, typed-nil Wrap, anemic entity; medium severity touching shared code, so after transport phases stabilize.

nodes.label: Phase 7: Infrastructure and Deploy Hygiene
nodes.rationale: .env never loaded on host, unknown APP_ENV accepted, Dockerfile gaps, MySQL infra lagging Postgres, RabbitMQ never closed.

nodes.label: Phase 8: gRPC Decision and Docs Honesty
nodes.rationale: Decide stub vs real gRPC transport, then do the final docs sweep once behavior is settled.
nodes.norm_label: phase 8: grpc decision and docs honesty

nodes.label: Phase 9: Close-out
nodes.rationale: The 2026-10-14 remediation review found phases marked done with exit criteria unmet and new High defects; fix them and replace grep-only proofs with behavior tests.

nodes.label: Phase 1 Plan: Generated Output Builds and Lints
nodes.rationale: Every supported `nova new` output builds, passes its own make lint, and is proven to do so by nova's test suite using the real toolchain.
nodes.norm_label: phase 1 plan: generated output builds and lints

nodes.label: gofmt-on-Write for Rendered Go (formatGoSource)
nodes.rationale: Conditional template lines drift struct alignment and import order (21 files), so a fresh project failed its own make lint, pre-commit hook and CI; formatting at write time in both generators fixes the whole class, and a parse failure surfaces a generator bug with the file name.

nodes.label: Real-Toolchain Bootstrap Proof (make gen -> go build -> golangci-lint run)
nodes.rationale: The vet matrix stubs dbgen and wire_gen, so only a real sqlc/wire/go build/golangci-lint run catches engine-specific DDL sqlc rejects or an injector wire cannot build; runs sequentially (each step near 1 GB) and skips when a tool is missing.
nodes.norm_label: real-toolchain bootstrap proof (make gen -> go build -> golangci-lint run)

nodes.label: Per-Engine users Migration DDL
nodes.rationale: MySQL projects could not build: the migration was Postgres DDL (BIGSERIAL, TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE), sqlc rejected it and dbgen never existed; MySQL now gets BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT and DATETIME(6), and the redundant email index is dropped because UNIQUE already indexes it.

nodes.label: In-Memory UserRepository for --database=none
nodes.rationale: Chosen over gating the User slice on HasDatabase: one template plus two DI lines keeps the CRUD demo runnable, while gating would thread a conditional through router, registrar, DI, OpenAPI and docs and leave a hollow project. Same error contract as SQL adapters (ErrNotFound, ErrAlreadyExists).

nodes.label: Gated Readiness Probe Body
nodes.rationale: No-DB projects failed on an unconditional probeCtx; with no downstream dependency Readiness reports the same process-up signal as Liveness.

nodes.label: make gen Order: sqlc -> tidy -> wire -> proto
nodes.rationale: sqlc must emit dbgen before go mod tidy can resolve its import, and wire needs a tidied module to type-check the injector; nextSteps, the generated Makefile and README now share this order, and WIRE_PATH uses `go env GOPATH`.
nodes.norm_label: make gen order: sqlc -> tidy -> wire -> proto

nodes.label: Generated Projects Pass Their Own golangci-lint
nodes.rationale: Template fixes for real lint hits: G115 int32 offset bound, errorlint errors.Is, nonamedreturns, perfsprint, ST1020, G101 false positive, embeddedstructfieldcheck, golines, gocognit, shadow, unconvert, and goimports local-prefixes set to the module; golines reformat-tags disabled.
nodes.norm_label: generated projects pass their own golangci-lint

nodes.label: Phase 2 Plan: CLI Hardening
nodes.rationale: nova new and nova add never silently produce a broken project, never destroy user files and never write outside the target directory; every advertised option is implemented or rejected before a file is written.

nodes.label: Single Option Registry and Validate Gate
nodes.rationale: Replaced three sources of truth (cmd/new.go help, prompt option lists, generator.New whitelists) that let --transport=cron, --config=toml, --query=raw etc. emit broken projects; one set of slices feeds flag help, prompts and Validate, which reports every problem at once. The never-implemented GRPCGateway field was removed.
nodes.norm_label: single option registry and validate gate

nodes.label: Validate Normalization of Engine-Dependent Fields
nodes.rationale: Empty Database/Cache/Search/MessageQueue become none, DBDriver defaults per engine, QueryGen defaults to sqlc, and both are blanked without a database so Makefile, nova.yaml and CLAUDE.md templates stop mentioning sqlc.

nodes.label: Flags().Changed for Boolean Flags
nodes.rationale: --docker=false was a no-op because applyFlags assigned only when true and DefaultConfig set true; testing Changed honours an explicit false, and --ci rejects values outside github/none.

nodes.label: Non-Empty Target Directory Guard (nova new --force)
nodes.rationale: Generate overwrites file by file and silently clobbered edits (e.g. internal/domain/user.go) in an existing directory.

nodes.label: nova add Go-Identifier Name Rule and Module Requirement
nodes.rationale: Names flow raw into file paths, package names and identifiers; ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*$ blocks traversal and non-parsing Go, and an empty module path would emit imports starting with a bare slash.
nodes.norm_label: nova add go-identifier name rule and module requirement

nodes.label: Output Path Confinement Under Project Root
nodes.rationale: filepath.Rel check so a hostile name or nova.yaml layout cannot write outside the project.
nodes.norm_label: output path confinement under project root

nodes.label: Feature-File Overwrite Guard (nova add --force)
nodes.rationale: Feature files are the user's to edit after generation; re-runs stop unless --force, while shared skipIfExists files are always left alone.

nodes.label: Skip Existing Create-Table Migration on Repository Re-run
nodes.norm_label: skip existing create-table migration on repository re-run

nodes.label: One Acronym-Aware Snake and Title in manifest
nodes.rationale: manifest.snake gave h_t_t_p_server while generator.snakeCase gave http_server, so file and table names diverged; one rule now drives the {snake} placeholder, sqlc table/column names and the mapper file name.
nodes.norm_label: one acronym-aware snake and title in manifest

nodes.label: Irregular Plural Rules for Table Names
nodes.rationale: plural appended s (categorys); now handles -y, -s, -x, -z, -ch, -sh endings; good enough for scaffolding.
nodes.norm_label: irregular plural rules for table names

nodes.label: --type Engine Match Guard
nodes.rationale: --type=mysql in a postgres project wrote an uncompilable repository and dropped MySQL DDL into the Postgres migrations dir.

nodes.label: Injectable io.Writer for Generator Progress Output
nodes.norm_label: injectable io.writer for generator progress output

nodes.label: Go AST Merge Helpers Moved to internal/gosrc
nodes.rationale: internal/generator mixed two generators, AST merge utilities and string-built codegen; MergeDecls keeps the semantics of mergeGoDecls.
nodes.norm_label: go ast merge helpers moved to internal/gosrc

nodes.label: Phase 3 Plan: Observability
nodes.rationale: From the logs alone an on-call engineer can answer where, when, what, who and why for every HTTP request, worker message and gRPC call. Deferred: otelpgx/redisotel spans, 2xx sampling knob, worker panic recovery and per-message timeout (phase 5).

nodes.label: Logger Renders Errors via AnErr
nodes.rationale: Every kv value went through zerolog Interface, so an error JSON-marshalled to {}; emit and With now type-switch error values to AnErr.

nodes.label: Service Identity Fields and RFC3339Nano Timestamps
nodes.rationale: service/version/env stamped on every line so aggregated logs identify the emitting process; sub-second timestamps keep lines within one second orderable; production level raised from warn to info so access and lifecycle lines stay visible.
nodes.norm_label: service identity fields and rfc3339nano timestamps

nodes.label: Redacted Config Summary (config loaded)
nodes.rationale: Config.Summary emits only fields present in this build with secrets omitted (the RabbitMQ URL is never logged) as the first log line of a process.

nodes.label: Canonical Log Field Names
nodes.rationale: err (never error), request_id, trace_id, user_id, route, path, duration_ms; removes the err vs error key drift.

nodes.label: Principal Slot (Auth -> Logging handoff)
nodes.rationale: identity.WithUserPrincipal derives a child context only inner handlers see, so the outer Logging middleware needs a mutable context slot (prepareAuthSlot/rememberPrincipal/principalFromSlot) to learn user_id; works for chi too.

nodes.label: Access Log route and user_id Fields
nodes.rationale: route is the pattern, path the raw path in all four frameworks; user_id comes from the principal slot.
nodes.norm_label: access log route and user_id fields

nodes.label: Inbound Request-ID Validation (ValidRequestID)
nodes.rationale: Inbound ids are reused only when 1-128 chars of [A-Za-z0-9._-]; otherwise replaced, so a hostile client cannot bloat log lines or smuggle delimiters into dashboards.

nodes.label: pkg/requestid Transport-Neutral Package
nodes.rationale: Deviation: rendering pkg/httputil for every project so worker and publishers could reach the request-id helpers leaked an HTTP package into worker and gRPC builds; the With/From/Valid plumbing moved to pkg/requestid and httputil is HTTP-only again.

nodes.label: Readiness Failure Warn Log
nodes.rationale: Logging skips probes, so a Warn on a failed /readyz is the only line a failing dependency produces.

nodes.label: OpenTelemetry Server-Span Middleware First in Chain
nodes.rationale: trace_id was empty on every line because no middleware started a span; otelfiber/otelgin/otelchi/otelecho installed first so RequestID and Logging see the server span; health probes filtered via isProbe. echo keeps deprecated contrib otelecho because the maintained module targets echo v5.
nodes.norm_label: opentelemetry server-span middleware first in chain

nodes.label: Broker-Neutral Worker Message and DispatchFunc
nodes.rationale: Message carries Topic, Payload, Key, Headers, Partition/Offset (Kafka) and DeliveryTag/MessageID (RabbitMQ) so dispatch can log broker position.

nodes.label: One Outcome Line per Worker Message
nodes.rationale: Worker-side counterpart of the HTTP access log: worker: message handled|failed with topic, partition/offset, request_id, trace_id, duration_ms and errors.LogFields; adopts the producer's trace context and request id. The per-feature handler's own line was removed so this is the single boundary log.
nodes.norm_label: one outcome line per worker message

nodes.label: Publisher Correlation Headers and Partition Key
nodes.rationale: correlationHeaders injects x-request-id and W3C trace context onto Kafka/RabbitMQ messages so consumer lines and spans join the producing HTTP request; sarama.StringEncoder(key) gives per-aggregate ordering.
nodes.norm_label: publisher correlation headers and partition key

nodes.label: Drain sarama Consumer Group Errors
nodes.rationale: Return.Errors is set, so undrained group.Errors() lose partition/offset/broker errors and eventually block.

nodes.label: gRPC Unary Interceptors and otelgrpc Stats Handler
nodes.rationale: The gRPC server had no interceptors at all; RequestID, Logging (server faults at error, client codes at warn) and Recovery (panic -> codes.Internal) mirror the HTTP middleware chain.
nodes.norm_label: grpc unary interceptors and otelgrpc stats handler

nodes.label: Runners Log Error Chain and Shutdown Duration
nodes.rationale: Runners use errors.LogFields and log shutdown complete with duration_ms; RunGRPCServer returns an error through cobra RunE for a non-zero exit; fx Stop and tracing shutdown errors are logged instead of discarded.
nodes.norm_label: runners log error chain and shutdown duration

nodes.label: Phase 4: HTTP Transport Parity and Security Plan
nodes.rationale: Every nova new HTTP project, whichever of fiber/gin/chi/echo it uses, must share one hardening contract: client IP only via trusted proxies, CORS never widened to '*', bounded body and request time, framework 404/405/413 in the standard envelope, RFC 6750/6585 credential endpoints, ownership on mutations, readiness without dependency error text. A framework with a native mechanism uses it; one without gets a prefixed middleware. Deliberately not done: a Redis-backed limiter, per-field validation errors, an admin role.
nodes.norm_label: phase 4: http transport parity and security plan

nodes.label: Trusted-proxy client IP resolution
nodes.rationale: X-Forwarded-For is honoured only from configured trusted proxies; with none the TCP peer is the client, so a client cannot spoof its address to the login limiter or the access log. Uses each framework's native mechanism (fiber TrustedProxies, gin SetTrustedProxies, echo IPExtractor with TrustPrivateNet(false)) because gin's default trusts every proxy and echo's default believes the header from anyone.

nodes.label: HTTPConfig.TrustedProxyNets()
nodes.rationale: Parses trusted_proxies (bare IP becomes /32 or /128); validated once in config.Load so routers may ignore the parse error and NewRouter keeps its signature.

nodes.label: chi middleware.ClientIP
nodes.rationale: chi has no native trusted-proxy mechanism, so a middleware resolves the client once (right-most XFF hop that is not a trusted proxy) and rewrites r.RemoteAddr to the bare IP; installed first so the span, limiter and access line all see the same address.

nodes.label: middleware.Timeout (per-request deadline)
nodes.rationale: Puts a deadline on every request context so a stalled dependency fails the request in the envelope (504) instead of holding the connection until the write timeout; request_timeout is kept below write_timeout. fiber cannot cancel on client disconnect, so this deadline is its only bound.

nodes.label: middleware.BodyLimit (http.MaxBytesReader)
nodes.rationale: gin, chi and echo lack fiber's BodyLimit config field; all three use net/http's MaxBytesReader (even echo, instead of its own BodyLimit) so the failure mode (*http.MaxBytesError, 413, connection closed) matches across frameworks.

nodes.label: httpwriter.bindError
nodes.rationale: Maps a body-decoding failure: over the configured limit is 413 PayloadTooLarge, anything else the generic 400 InvalidRequest.

nodes.label: CORS never widens to *
nodes.rationale: fiber's and echo's CORS middleware treat an empty origin list as '*', so an empty list installs nothing; gin and chi add Vary: Origin on every response so caches never serve one origin's answer to another.

nodes.label: errors.FromStatus / statusLocale
nodes.rationale: Framework-raised statuses (router 404/405, server 413) map to a canonical locale code and the same envelope as application errors; a status with no canonical code becomes 500 so a framework error can never leak an unmapped status or its own text. The framework error is attached with WithCause so it still reaches the access log.

nodes.label: context.DeadlineExceeded to 504 classification
nodes.rationale: The request deadline or a dependency's own timeout expiring means the upstream did not answer in time, classified as 504 GatewayTimeout in pkg/errors.

nodes.label: httpwriter.HandleError (fiber ErrorHandler / echo HTTPErrorHandler)
nodes.rationale: Every error escaping the handler chain is written in the standard envelope; framework errors (*fiber.Error, *echo.HTTPError) map by status through errors.FromStatus. echo leaves an already-committed response alone.

nodes.label: Access log resolves handler errors inline
nodes.rationale: fiber and echo would run their error handler after the logging middleware returns, so the access line would read 200; resolving the error inside the access-log scope makes the logged status the one the client receives, and the level follows the status alone. gin/chi instead route unknown paths/methods via NoRoute/NoMethod and NotFound/MethodNotAllowed.
nodes.norm_label: access log resolves handler errors inline

nodes.label: RFC 6750 bearer challenge (WWW-Authenticate)
nodes.rationale: The bearer scheme is compared case-insensitively (RFC 9110 section 11.1); a missing credential gets the bare 'Bearer' challenge and a rejected one 'Bearer error="invalid_token"' on every 401.

nodes.label: LoginRateLimit ipLimiter (TTL eviction, Retry-After)
nodes.rationale: Per-IP token buckets idle past visitorTTL (10 min) are swept every minute so memory is bounded by recent clients; a refusal sets Retry-After (RFC 6585). A second instance guards registration with its own budget. Per-process: N replicas allow N times the limit; global limiting belongs upstream.

nodes.label: security.MaxPasswordLen = 72
nodes.rationale: bcrypt hashes only the first 72 bytes and rejects longer input, so the usecase refuses longer passwords up front (400) instead of failing with a 500.

nodes.label: usecase requireSelf ownership check
nodes.rationale: Lives in the usecase rather than the handler so every transport applies the same rule on Update/Delete: no principal is 401, another user's id is 403. Widen it (roles, admin audience) here when needed.

nodes.label: Service.timingHash (login timing equalizer)
nodes.rationale: An unknown-email login verifies against a dummy bcrypt hash so wall-clock time matches the bad-password path (no enumeration oracle). Built on first use under a mutex and fails closed if hashing fails, replacing the package-level dummyHashOnce that could leave an empty hash.

nodes.label: health.Checker.Readiness returning (Status, error)
nodes.rationale: The readiness body names each dependency 'ok' or 'fail' so an anonymous caller learns which one is down but never its error text; the joined error is logged by the router instead.

nodes.label: OpenAPI document rewritten from handlers
nodes.rationale: Fixes OpenAPI drift: page/perPage/email and cursor/limit lists, requestId on every envelope, PageMeta/CursorMeta, WWW-Authenticate on 401, Retry-After on 429, 413 on POST bodies, 403 on PUT/DELETE, password maxLength 72, probe details ok/fail.

nodes.label: http_chi_postgres_fx standing bootstrap case
nodes.rationale: Replaced the planned one-off chi bootstrap so every framework gets a real golangci-lint run; it showed chi's Logging middleware had been over the gocognit limit since phase 3.

nodes.label: Phase 5: Worker Reliability and Messaging Plan
nodes.rationale: A worker project on Kafka or RabbitMQ handles every message under one policy (per-attempt deadline, panic guard, bounded retries with backoff, then parking on a dead-letter topic/queue), settles each delivery identically on both brokers, exits non-zero when the broker side disappears, drains its in-flight message before closing the consumer, records each event exactly once, and publishes to the exchange the worker actually binds.
nodes.norm_label: phase 5: worker reliability and messaging plan

nodes.label: worker.Policy
nodes.rationale: HandlerTimeout, MaxAttempts and RetryBackoff; the zero value takes defaults (30s, 3, 500ms) so a worker built without configuration still has a deadline, a retry budget and a parking rule.

nodes.label: Worker.run / Worker.attempt retry loop
nodes.rationale: Each attempt gets its own deadline and panic guard; transient failures retry with doubling backoff; poison or an exhausted budget comes back wrapped in ErrParked; a cancelled ctx returns ctx.Err() so the consumer leaves the message for redelivery.

nodes.label: worker.Poison / ErrPoison
nodes.rationale: Handlers wrap input that can never succeed (malformed JSON, missing eventId) so it is parked without retrying, instead of being retried forever or silently acked and dropped.

nodes.label: worker.ErrParked
nodes.rationale: Returned by dispatch once a message is given up on (poison or MaxAttempts exhausted); consumers copy it to the dead-letter topic/queue and ack the original so the stream keeps moving.

nodes.label: worker.ErrConsumerClosed
nodes.rationale: Returned by Subscribe when the broker side ended the subscription while ctx was still live, so RunWorker exits non-zero and the orchestrator restarts the process.

nodes.label: worker.ErrHandlerPanic
nodes.rationale: Wraps a recovered handler panic so one bad message cannot take the process down; counts as a failed attempt.

nodes.label: Dispatch outcomes: handled, parked, abandoned
nodes.rationale: dispatch returns nil to ack, an error wrapping ErrParked to dead-letter then ack, or the ctx error to leave the message for redelivery; both brokers settle these three outcomes the same way.

nodes.label: kafkaConsumer and kafkaSessionHandler.settle
nodes.rationale: ConsumeClaim never returns on a handler error (returning ends the session and triggers a rebalance, so one poison message no longer rebalances the group); the offset is marked only once a message is handled or parked on <topic>.dlq through the shared sync producer; abandoned messages stay unmarked; a closed group while ctx is live becomes ErrConsumerClosed.

nodes.label: rabbitmqConsumer (Qos, NotifyClose, dead-letter exchange)
nodes.rationale: Declares the topology so the worker boots before the publisher; Qos bounds the unacked backlog a slow handler can hold; NotifyClose surfaces channel/connection errors as ErrConsumerClosed; settles handled as Ack, parked as Nack(requeue=false) to the DLX, abandoned as Nack(requeue=true) so another replica gets it.

nodes.label: Dead-letter wire contract (.dlq, .dlx, x-dead-letter-reason/source)
nodes.rationale: Fixed wire names: Kafka copies parked messages to <topic>.dlq with the original headers plus reason and <topic>/<partition>/<offset> source so they can be inspected or replayed (original key keeps per-aggregate order); RabbitMQ queues dead-letter via x-dead-letter-exchange to <exchange>.dlx, whose only queue is <queue>.dlq.

nodes.label: config.RabbitMQConfig (Exchange, Queue, Prefetch)
nodes.rationale: The exchange is shared by the publisher and the worker so a published message is routable to the queue the worker declares; Queue and Prefetch are worker-only. Topic names are wire contracts owned by handlers and publisher, so UserCreatedTopic/UserCreatedQueue config was deleted.

nodes.label: config.WorkerConfig
nodes.rationale: handler_timeout, max_attempts and retry_backoff in base.yaml (worker projects only), bounding how the consumer handles one message.

nodes.label: di.provideWorkerPolicy
nodes.rationale: Projects the worker config onto the transport's Policy so transport/worker stays free of the config package; the nova add skel variant returns the zero value (defaults).

nodes.label: RabbitMQ Publisher (confirm mode, persistent messages)
nodes.rationale: Confirm mode means a publish that returns nil was accepted by the broker, not just written to the socket; persistent delivery survives a broker restart like the durable queue it lands in; returns a cleanup that closes its channel while the connection has its own cleanup.

nodes.label: UserCreatedMessage.EventID / x-event-id header
nodes.rationale: A producer-minted uuid is the consumer's idempotency key: a redelivery carries the same id and is recorded once. Both brokers carry it as the x-event-id header (RabbitMQ also as MessageId).

nodes.label: RunWorker drain and zombie exit
nodes.rationale: A consume loop that returns while ctx is live (nil or ErrConsumerClosed) is fatal and exits non-zero because nothing resubscribes in-process; on shutdown it waits up to drainTimeout (30s) for the in-flight message so the last ack or offset commit lands before Stop().

nodes.label: domain.ErrEventAlreadyRecorded
nodes.rationale: The audit repository reports a redelivered event (zero rows inserted) as this sentinel; the useraudit service treats the delivery as done and logs one 'duplicate delivery ignored' line.

nodes.label: Idempotent user_audit_log insert (event_id unique index)
nodes.rationale: The broker delivers at least once; a unique index on event_id plus ON CONFLICT (event_id) DO NOTHING (postgres) or ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE id = id (mysql) with sqlc :execrows turns a redelivery into a no-op insert detectable by row count.

nodes.label: Generated broker-less worker tests
nodes.rationale: worker_test.go (TestDispatchOutcomes, abandon-on-shutdown, unknown topic, zero-value policy) and consumer_test.go (TestKafkaSettle with sarama mocks, TestRabbitMQHandle with a fake Acknowledger) ship with the project; the bootstrap runs them so they are proven, not just compiled.

nodes.label: worker_mysql_rabbitmq_fx bootstrap case
nodes.rationale: RabbitMQ, MySQL and fx had no real toolchain run; the sixth bootstrap executes the RabbitMQ consumer tests and real sqlc on the MySQL ON DUPLICATE KEY query.

nodes.label: Phase 6: Layers and Domain Correctness Plan
nodes.rationale: A nova new project must obey its own dependency rule (no usecase to infrastructure import), never return a typed-nil *AppError, answer a concurrent duplicate registration with 409 not 500, run Register and List inside the transaction manager, enforce user invariants in the entity, report the real UpdatedAt, start without Redis with jittered cache TTLs, carry only identity claims, register translations once, and use golang-jwt/jwt/v5.
nodes.norm_label: phase 6: layers and domain correctness plan

nodes.label: security.TokenIssuer port
nodes.rationale: Replaces the concrete *jwtsec.TokenService in the usecase so it imports no infrastructure. Only signing is a port because only login needs it; verification is a transport (middleware) concern that calls infrastructure/jwt directly. Bound in DI with wire.Bind or the fx caster provideTokenIssuer.

nodes.label: jwtsec.TokenService on golang-jwt v5
nodes.rationale: Moves to v5 parser options (WithValidMethods, WithExpirationRequired, WithIssuer, WithAudience) so a token minted for another environment fails like any other bad token, replacing the manual VerifyIssuer/VerifyAudience block; classifyParseError uses v5 sentinel errors and treats anything unrecognised as anomalous so it never hides in the noise.

nodes.label: errors.Wrap/Wrapf return error (typed-nil fix)
nodes.rationale: A nil *AppError stored in an error interface is non-nil, so Wrap/Wrapf now return error and Wrap(nil) yields a true nil, making 'return errors.Wrap(err, ...)' safe unconditionally. L, FromStatus and WithCause keep returning *AppError because they never return nil and WithCause chaining needs the concrete type.

nodes.label: locale.NewMapping guarded by sync.Once
nodes.rationale: NewMapping is called from the DI provider and from tests; a second registration must not race the first reader.

nodes.label: domain.TxManager in Register and List
nodes.rationale: Hash outside the transaction (bcrypt ~100ms must not hold a connection open); uniqueness check plus insert run inside WithinTx; List runs page plus count in one transaction so both come from one snapshot where isolation provides it (MySQL REPEATABLE READ does, Postgres READ COMMITTED does not).

nodes.label: memory.TxManager (no-op)
nodes.rationale: The in-memory repository has no transaction to open, but ships a no-op TxManager so the usecase can depend on the port whichever storage is wired.

nodes.label: translate: unique violation to ErrAlreadyExists
