nodes.rationale: Two registrations can pass the uniqueness check together; the unique index decides. Each SQL adapter maps SQLSTATE 23505 (pgx) or MySQL 1062 to errors.ErrAlreadyExists while keeping the driver error in the chain, and the usecase maps that to locale.UserEmailExists, so the client gets 409 instead of 500.

nodes.label: entity.NewUser / User.Rename invariants
nodes.rationale: Email must parse as an address and the name must be 2 to 100 runes; living in the entity rather than request-validation tags means every transport (HTTP, gRPC, worker, a future CLI) inherits them. Rename stamps UpdatedAt and UpdateUser now writes updated_at, so the persisted row and the response agree.

nodes.label: cache.New starts degraded without Redis
nodes.rationale: Redis is a cache: reads fall through to the database and readiness reports it as 'fail' until it is back, so an unreachable cache logs a warning instead of keeping the process from booting.

nodes.label: User cache decorator: jittered TTL and soft invalidation
nodes.rationale: Up to 3 minutes of TTL jitter so a cold start does not expire every key at once; a failed DEL after a successful write logs a warning and relies on the TTL, since failing the request would not make the cache fresher.
nodes.norm_label: user cache decorator: jittered ttl and soft invalidation

nodes.label: Identity-only UserPrincipal and access-token claims
nodes.rationale: Device, session, platform and phone fields are dropped from the principal and AccessTokenClaims; add claims as the token grows (e.g. a session id for refresh tokens).

nodes.label: Generated unit tests (errors, usecase fakes, adapter translation)
nodes.rationale: TestWrapNilIsNil, TestRegisterDuplicateEmailIs409, TestUpdateReportsNewUpdatedAt, TestLoginSignsThroughThePort and TestTranslateUniqueViolation ship with the project; the bootstrap runs ./pkg, ./internal/usecase and ./internal/adapter tests so they are proven, not just compiled.
nodes.norm_label: generated unit tests (errors, usecase fakes, adapter translation)

nodes.label: Phase 7: Infrastructure and Deploy Hygiene Plan
nodes.rationale: A fresh nova new project should boot on the host from cp .env.example .env, reject a misspelled APP_ENV, configure MySQL as fully as Postgres, build a reproducible port-driven image, ship pinned hermetic CI, make fx shutdown tunable, serve its own OpenAPI document and document the costs it cannot remove.
nodes.norm_label: phase 7: infrastructure and deploy hygiene plan

nodes.label: loadDotEnv (.env loading on host runs)
nodes.rationale: Makes cp .env.example .env && go run main.go api work; real environment variables always win (godotenv.Load never overrides) and a missing file is not an error because containers inject env and ship no .env.

nodes.label: APP_ENV whitelist (local, development, production)
nodes.rationale: A typo must not silently run with base defaults (ssl_mode: disable, debug-friendly limits) in what the operator believes is production.

nodes.label: DB_USER required check
nodes.rationale: Without DB_USER the driver falls back to the OS user, which looks like a database permissions bug; fail with the real cause instead.

nodes.label: Config.ShutdownTimeout (shutdown_timeout, APP_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT)
nodes.rationale: Bounds the whole cleanup chain (server drain then dependency closes); default 20s, kept above the http/grpc shutdown_timeout.

nodes.label: Config-driven fx stop budget
nodes.rationale: Replaces the stopTimeout const so an operator can widen the budget when a dependency close is slow; a stop that overruns it is logged with timeout_ms so skipped hooks are visible, not silently dropped.

nodes.label: MySQL TLS, lifetime and connect_timeout knobs (NewMySQLDB)
nodes.rationale: MySQL configured like Postgres: tls skip-verify is the counterpart of sslmode=require, connection lifetimes mirror the pgx pool, and connect_timeout bounds both the dial and the startup ping.
nodes.norm_label: mysql tls, lifetime and connect_timeout knobs (newmysqldb)

nodes.label: Cobra root SilenceUsage
nodes.rationale: A boot failure prints the error, not the usage text.

nodes.label: Port-driven Dockerfile on alpine:3.22 with -trimpath
nodes.rationale: One knob for the port: the SERVER_PORT/GRPC_PORT build arg drives ENV, EXPOSE and the /readyz healthcheck; -trimpath makes the binary reproducible without leaked host paths; the dead config COPY is dropped because the YAML is embedded.

nodes.label: .dockerignore template
nodes.rationale: Keeps the build context to what the image needs: no secrets (.env), no local state, no git history.

nodes.label: Pinned, hermetic generated CI (golangci-lint-action@v8, v2.11.4)
nodes.rationale: The golden config is a v2 config and the v6 action only drove v1; rendered tests are hermetic (fakes, hand-built driver errors), so service containers and env are dropped; build uses -trimpath.

nodes.label: wire as a go tool dependency
nodes.norm_label: wire as a go tool dependency

nodes.label: Embedded OpenAPI document served at GET /openapi.yaml
nodes.rationale: The running service serves its own contract so tooling fetches it from the same binary that implements it.
nodes.norm_label: embedded openapi document served at get /openapi.yaml

nodes.label: Kafka producer dials at startup (deliberate)
nodes.rationale: A publisher that cannot reach its broker is misconfiguration and compose waits on the broker's healthcheck, so the dial stays eager (unlike Redis) and is documented in docs 09 rather than made lazy.

nodes.label: Elasticsearch lint cost (Search off in bootstrap)
nodes.rationale: --search=elasticsearch makes golangci-lint run take 6-8 min vs 19 s because of the typed client's generated types; documented in docs 01 rather than switching clients, and the bootstrap keeps Search off.
nodes.norm_label: elasticsearch lint cost (search off in bootstrap)

nodes.label: Pinned external tool versions (sqlc v1.30.0, migrate v4.19.0, sqlfluff 4.2.2, golangci-lint v2.11.4)
nodes.norm_label: pinned external tool versions (sqlc v1.30.0, migrate v4.19.0, sqlfluff 4.2.2, golangci-lint v2.11.4)

nodes.label: Phase 8: gRPC Decision and Docs Honesty Plan
nodes.rationale: --transport=grpc should produce a working service (proto contract, buf stubs, health, reflection, bearer auth, HTTP-equivalent error classification) and every doc claim from the 2026-10-04 review should be confirmed against rendered output by a test.
nodes.norm_label: phase 8: grpc decision and docs honesty plan

nodes.label: Decision: gRPC as a real transport (option a)
nodes.rationale: Everything around the service was already real after phases 3 and 7 and nova ships a gen-grpc target; labelling the one missing piece experimental would leave a server that listens and answers nothing. The cost is one phase.
nodes.norm_label: decision: grpc as a real transport (option a)

nodes.label: UserService proto contract (user.v1)
nodes.rationale: One RPC per HTTP endpoint (CreateUser, Login, GetUser, UpdateUser, DeleteUser, ListUsers, ListPublicUsers); CreateUser, Login and ListPublicUsers are public.

nodes.label: buf generate with go-run-pinned protoc plugins
nodes.rationale: protoc-gen-go v1.36.12 and protoc-gen-go-grpc v1.6.2 run as version-pinned go run invocations, so buf v1.70.0 is the only tool to install and the pins live only in buf.gen.yaml and the README.
nodes.norm_label: buf generate with go-run-pinned protoc plugins

nodes.label: make gen order: sqlc-gen, proto-gen, tidy, wire-gen
nodes.rationale: One tidy: tidy tolerates the missing generated package and go tool cannot run before tidy; generated api/gen is committed like dbgen and wire_gen.go because the Dockerfile and CI assume it.
nodes.norm_label: make gen order: sqlc-gen, proto-gen, tidy, wire-gen

nodes.label: transportgrpc.New gRPC server factory
nodes.rationale: Mirrors transport/http.NewRouter: interceptor order RequestID, Locale, Logging, Recovery, Auth so an auth failure is logged and any panic is recovered; registers feature Registrars, health and optional reflection; unary-only until the first streaming RPC.

nodes.label: gRPC Registrar interface (Register, Protected)
nodes.rationale: One feature's gRPC surface: registers its generated service and names the full methods that need a bearer token (the HTTP Registrar's Auth group, per method).

nodes.label: rpcstatus.FromError
nodes.rationale: The gRPC counterpart of httpwriter.WriteError: classify once through pkg/errors, stash the AppError for the access log, translate the client message; internal text never reaches the client.

nodes.label: codeFor HTTP-status-to-gRPC-code mapping
nodes.rationale: Maps the HTTP status pkg/errors assigns to the nearest gRPC code so one classification table serves both transports.

nodes.label: gRPC Auth interceptor (bearer token in authorization metadata)
nodes.rationale: Verifies the bearer token only on protected full methods and attaches identity.UserPrincipal; a missing or rejected token is Unauthenticated with the localized HTTP 401 message.
nodes.norm_label: grpc auth interceptor (bearer token in authorization metadata)

nodes.label: gRPC Logging interceptor AppError stash
nodes.rationale: PrepareAppErrorContext before the handler and AppErrorFromContext after it, so the access line carries the cause and frame trail, not the status text.

nodes.label: NewGRPCServer flips health to NOT_SERVING before GracefulStop
nodes.rationale: NOT_SERVING first so health-checking balancers stop routing while in-flight calls drain; health reports process liveness, not dependency readiness.
nodes.norm_label: newgrpcserver flips health to not_serving before gracefulstop

nodes.label: GRPCConfig.Reflection flag (on in base, off in production)
nodes.rationale: Reflection lets grpcurl discover services; it is turned off in production.
nodes.norm_label: grpcconfig.reflection flag (on in base, off in production)

nodes.label: Rendered gRPC end-to-end tests over bufconn
nodes.rationale: TestUserServiceEndToEnd, TestHealthFollowsLifecycle and TestAcceptLanguageTranslates drive the real server over bufconn with a fake repo and a real JWT token service.
nodes.norm_label: rendered grpc end-to-end tests over bufconn

nodes.label: int64 pagination fields in proto (deviation)
nodes.rationale: gosec G115 flags every int to int32 narrowing in the handler; widening the wire type removes the conversions instead of silencing them.

nodes.label: gRPC Recovery interceptor via closure (deviation)
nodes.rationale: Named returns are rejected by nonamedreturns now that a gRPC project is linted for the first time, so it recovers through a closure like the worker does.

nodes.label: Docs honesty guarded by a test
nodes.rationale: Every doc claim the 2026-10-04 review flagged is checked against rendered output so a doc and a template cannot drift apart silently again.
nodes.norm_label: docs honesty guarded by a test

nodes.label: Phase 9: Close-out Plan
nodes.rationale: Close the roadmap: fix the four High and twelve Medium defects from the 2026-10-14 remediation review, replace grep-only HTTP parity proof with rendered behavior tests, cover every gen-* combination, make the fourteen false doc claims true, and run nova's own tests in CI.

nodes.label: Validate normalizations and empty DefaultConfig module/driver
nodes.rationale: HTTPFramework defaults to fiber for HTTP and is blanked otherwise, the driver defaults per engine, worker without a SQL database is rejected, and DefaultConfig stops pre-filling ModuleName/DBDriver; an explicit --http-framework on a non-HTTP transport is rejected rather than silently blanked.
nodes.norm_label: validate normalizations and empty defaultconfig module/driver

nodes.label: nova add worker refuses a non-kafka/rabbitmq broker
nodes.norm_label: nova add worker refuses a non-kafka/rabbitmq broker

nodes.label: Fiber ClientIP middleware (RemoteIP)
nodes.rationale: Walks X-Forwarded-For right to left past trusted proxies the way chi already does and stores a copied string; the router drops ProxyHeader/EnableTrustedProxyCheck/TrustedProxies so c.IP() is the TCP peer, and the limiter and access line use RemoteIP.

nodes.label: RabbitMQ shared default exchange events and <queue>.dlx
nodes.rationale: Publisher and worker meet on one default exchange; naming the dead-letter exchange after the queue keeps queue arguments stable when the work exchange changes.
nodes.norm_label: rabbitmq shared default exchange events and <queue>.dlx

nodes.label: Compose Kafka listeners (kafka:29092 in-network, localhost:9092 host)
nodes.rationale: Moving the host listener to 9092 makes .env.example correct; listeners bind with empty hosts because Kafka 3.9 refuses an advertised 0.0.0.0 controller listener, and the healthcheck probes the in-network listener.
nodes.norm_label: compose kafka listeners (kafka:29092 in-network, localhost:9092 host)

nodes.label: Kafka park retries dead-letter write with capped backoff
nodes.rationale: Backoff 100 ms doubling to 30 s until the session ends; settle never returns an error so ConsumeClaim ends only on shutdown instead of looping rejoins.
nodes.norm_label: kafka park retries dead-letter write with capped backoff

nodes.norm_label: loaddotenv sets only non-empty unset values; list entries trimmed

nodes.norm_label: nova new --force reuses existing migration name

nodes.label: gRPC deny-by-default auth (Public(), Throttled())
nodes.rationale: Registrar becomes Register, Public(), Throttled(); Auth protects every method outside the public set (health Check always public) instead of opt-in Protected().

nodes.label: gRPC Throttle interceptor (per-peer token bucket on Login and CreateUser)
